text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since the newborn had no prenatal care and immunization records are unavailable, what specific physical examination findings or symptoms are you observing in the infant right now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a continuous heart murmur, congenital cataracts, and sensorineural hearing loss is highly suggestive of Congenital Rubella Syndrome. Given the lack of prenatal care, have there been any reports of maternal rash, fever, or joint pain during the first trimester of pregnancy?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no past medical history available. Social history: Mother is a primigravida, no prenatal care received.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical triad of cataracts, deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus (continuous murmur) is classic for Congenital Rubella Syndrome. To confirm the diagnosis and assess for other potential complications, I will request specific diagnostic testing.

REQUEST TEST: Rubella_Specific_IgM_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text:
The positive Rubella-specific IgM antibody test confirms the diagnosis of Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
